registered_before: any overhead measurement of the current probe (the earlier overhead code was retired 18/10)
question: What does Pulse's eBPF counting cost per syscall, for monitored and for unmonitored processes on the same node?
probe: pulse_counter_extended (raw_tp/sys_enter on every syscall of the node, per-cgroup counters, 64 syscall bins, 64 transition bins, per-thread last syscall; fexit/__seccomp_filter), the object the live workers attach

conditions.filtered: probe attached, benchmark cgroup not in the allow list
conditions.monitored: probe attached, benchmark cgroup in the allow list

workload: testbed/bench/syscall_bench.c, static: getpid (near-null), read4k (/dev/zero), openclose (/tmp), mmapunmap; 10 s per mode, in a dedicated cgroup /sys/fs/cgroup/pulse-bench
design: 5 rounds on one worker; the three conditions rotate their order every round; 3 s settle after attaching
preconditions: no live run, the 1 s collector stopped, no other Pulse loader attached (the runner refuses otherwise); Tetragon and the cluster stay as in normal operation
metrics: median ns/op per condition and mode
relative overhead filtered/off and monitored/off as the median of per-round paired ratios with a bootstrap 95 % CI over rounds
complements: end-to-end cost already measured in live runs: worker CPU 13-31 % of one core with fast scoring (SENTINEL_PULSE_STATUS 5.8), RCA/Tetragon cost (RCA report)
limits: microbenchmark: a lower bound on the share for syscall-light applications and an upper bound for syscall-heavy ones; one worker, one kernel (Ubuntu 24.04, 6.8.0)
